text: Carrots are food and pots are not food, so starting with We, what do we eat?
We eat carrots.
Now the card shows stones instead of carrots, so starting with We, what do we say about eating stones?
We do not eat stones.
Pots are not food, so can you find and fix one word in this sentence?
We do not eat pots.
Potatoes are food and stones are not food, so how can you say what we eat in a full sentence starting with We?
We eat potatoes.
A pot is not food, so how can you tell us about eating pots in a full sentence starting with We?
We do not eat pots.
Onions are food and stones are not food, so can you use but to tell us about eating both things in one sentence?
We eat onions, but we do not eat stones.
Your group has no onions, so how can you describe this starting with We?
We do not have any onions.
Your group needs onions, so can you ask Lee about onions using a question that starts with Do you?
Do you have any onions?
You want to ask Kim about carrots, so can you fix one word in the question?
Do you have any carrots?
You do not know if Kim has food, so how can you ask her group about food starting with Do you?
Do you have any food?
Your group has no potatoes and Lee asks about them, so how can you answer in a full sentence starting with We?
We do not have any potatoes.
Starting with We, how can you answer a question about the three sausages your group has?
We have three sausages.
In this story, getting paper comes first and showing the picture comes last, so starting with The girl, what happens in the middle?
The girl draws a tree in the middle.
Now two girls make the picture together, so starting with The girls, what do they do at the end?
The girls show the picture at the end.
The boy's first action is to draw a house, so can you fix one word in this sentence about the beginning?
The boy draws a house at the beginning.
Two children get a pot, add water, and then add carrots, so can you tell us the beginning in a full sentence starting with They?
They get a pot at the beginning.
A boy gets paper, draws a cat, and shows the picture, so can you tell us the middle in a full sentence starting with The boy?
The boy draws a cat in the middle.
Two children get a pot, add food, and eat soup, so can you tell us the ending in a full sentence starting with They?
They eat soup at the end.
Can you start with the word they and tell us the total number of potatoes, if Leo has three and Mia has five?
They have eight potatoes.
Now it is your turn to ask about their total number of potatoes, so how can you ask a question starting with How many?
How many potatoes do they have?
Look at the vegetables on both cards and their combined number, then find and fix one word in the sentence.
They have seven carrots.
Can you start with the word they and tell us the total number of sausages, if Ben has two and Anna has five?
They have seven sausages.
You want to know the number of onions in Mia's basket, so how can you ask her starting with How many?
How many onions do you have?
There are three carrots and two more carrots in the pot, but four carrots stay in a bowl, so starting with There, how many are in the pot?
There are five carrots in the pot.
In this story your group is hungry and has no food, so how can you explain why using We and because?
We are hungry because we have no food.
Now your group has food and is not hungry, so how can you explain the change using We and because?
We are not hungry because we have food.
With soup for lunch, these two children are not hungry, so can you fix one word in this sentence about why?
They are not hungry because they have soup.
This boy is hungry and has no food, so how can you explain why using He and because?
He is hungry because he has no food.
These children have soup and are not hungry, so how can you explain why using They and because?
They are not hungry because they have soup.
The children share one pot of soup so that everyone gets some, so how can you explain this using Everyone and because?
Everyone has soup because they share.
